title: Singular partitive in absence statements
summary: Use singular partitive for an absent thing in a location statement: Pöydällä ei ole kirjaa. — There is no book on the table.
prerequisiteSkills: An activity in progress: singular object
objectives: Use singular partitive for the absent thing in a simple location statement.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Use singular partitive for the absent thing in a simple location statement.
A location comes first, followed by ei ole and the absent item. These complete location forms are supplied. The statement introduces absence rather than describing an already identified subject.
Negative possession uses a related familiar pattern. Its owner forms remain taught in the existing possession pack and are not an additional target here.
keyPoints: In this there-is-no construction, the absent thing or substance uses singular partitive. Keep the fixed ei ole frame.

examples.english: There is no book on the table.
steps: In this there-is-no construction, the absent thing or substance uses singular partitive. Keep the fixed ei ole frame.
Pöydällä means “on the table” and works as the location. pöytä uses the weak stem pöydä- (t → d) plus -llä: pöydällä.
ei means “not” and works as the verb. ei comes from ei: the third-person singular negative verb ei.
ole means “be” and works as the verb. ole comes from olla: the negative main-verb form ole, without a person ending.
kirjaa means “book” and works as the singular partitive noun naming the present or absent item. Keep kirja and add -a: kirja + a = kirjaa.

examples.english: There is no toy in the box.
steps: In this there-is-no construction, the absent thing or substance uses singular partitive. Keep the fixed ei ole frame.
Laatikossa means “in the box” and works as the location. laatikko uses the weak stem laatiko- (kk → k) plus -ssa: laatikossa.
ei means “not” and works as the verb. ei comes from ei: the third-person singular negative verb ei.
ole means “be” and works as the verb. ole comes from olla: the negative main-verb form ole, without a person ending.
lelua means “toy” and works as the singular partitive noun naming the present or absent item. Keep lelu and add -a because u is a back vowel: lelua.

examples.english: There is no cup on the table.
steps: In this there-is-no construction, the absent thing or substance uses singular partitive. Keep the fixed ei ole frame.
Pöydällä means “on the table” and works as the location. pöytä uses the weak stem pöydä- (t → d) plus -llä: pöydällä.
ei means “not” and works as the verb. ei comes from ei: the third-person singular negative verb ei.
ole means “be” and works as the verb. ole comes from olla: the negative main-verb form ole, without a person ending.
kuppia means “cup” and works as the singular partitive noun naming the present or absent item. Keep strong pp and the final i: kuppi + a = kuppia.

examples.english: There is no ball in the box.
steps: In this there-is-no construction, the absent thing or substance uses singular partitive. Keep the fixed ei ole frame.
Laatikossa means “in the box” and works as the location. laatikko uses the weak stem laatiko- (kk → k) plus -ssa: laatikossa.
ei means “not” and works as the verb. ei comes from ei: the third-person singular negative verb ei.
ole means “be” and works as the verb. ole comes from olla: the negative main-verb form ole, without a person ending.
palloa means “ball” and works as the singular partitive noun naming the present or absent item. Keep pallo unchanged and add -a: palloa.

commonMistakes: Keep ei ole fixed in the supplied absence frame.
Do not apply the construction mechanically to an identity statement.
